None of the three solutions appears to be correct. I'll explain why and then pick the least wrong one.

**Setup.** The bricks in a layer are identical. Layer n has m = 2^n − 1 bricks and layer n+1 has 2m + 1 bricks. The natural reading is that every layer spans the full width of the wall, so a brick in layer n has width 1/m.

**Which bricks a brick touches.** Number the bricks in each layer from 0. Brick i in layer n covers [i/m, (i+1)/m]. Brick j in layer n+1 covers [j/(2m+1), (j+1)/(2m+1)]. A shared side needs a positive-length overlap, which gives the conditions

- j < (i+1)(2m+1)/m = 2i + 2 + (i+1)/m,
- j + 1 > i(2m+1)/m = 2i + i/m.

Since 0 < (i+1)/m ≤ 1, the first condition gives j ≤ 2i + 2. Since 0 ≤ i/m < 1, the second gives j ≥ 2i. So the touching bricks are exactly j = 2i, 2i+1, 2i+2, and all three exist because 2i+2 ≤ 2m. Every brick therefore has exactly 3 choices below it.

**Count.** Jessica makes 2025 moves, each with 3 choices, so the number of sequences is 3^2025.

**Checking the solutions.**
- Solution 1 gives 2^2025. It assumes a half-brick offset between layers, which does not match the layer sizes.
- Solution 2 gives 1. It forces the bricks into aligned columns of unit width, which ignores that the layers have different brick counts.
- Solution 3 gives C(2025, 1012). It assumes a running-bond pattern, which does not match the layer sizes either.

I did not verify the numeric values of the final answers, since the derivations already differ from 3^2025.

CHOICE: 1
